Subject: Post-call recap + quantization trade study (AWQ/GPTQ/FP8) - next steps

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from discovery:
- Primary workload: customer service summarization + policy classification across long documents (avg 1200 tokens)
- SLA targets: 200 ms p99 for short replies, 500 ms p95 for longer summarization paths
- Constraint: FinWave prefers lower-cost inference for high throughput daytime traffic and higher-quality evening batch runs
- Hardware: currently planning H100 on Dedicated cluster for initial rollout (may add A100 later)

Model fit / recommended eval plan:
- Baseline models to evaluate: Llama-3-13B, Mistral-7B-Instruct, Llama-3-70B (as high-quality reference)
- Quantization variants to test: AWQ (4-bit), GPTQ (4-bit), FP8 (where supported)
- Prompt sets: attached prompt_set_finwave_v2.txt — includes production prompts + edge cases and a small regression set we flagged
- Proposed metrics: exact-match classification, Rouge-L for summarization, response latency (p50/p95/p99), and manual quality scoring (1-5) on 200 samples

Initial trade-offs we discussed:
- AWQ often preserves higher quality on instruction-tuned Llama variants at 3/4-bit relative to GPTQ, at modest throughput cost
- GPTQ is broadly supported and typically yields good speedups; may show slightly lower quality on some instruction tasks without per-layer tuning
- FP8 offers strong throughput improvements on H100 with often minimal quality regression vs full-float for many models, but requires H100-compatible runtime and is less portable to older GPUs

Attachments / links: finwave_quant_tradeoffs_v1.pdf (quick slide trade-off), finwave_eval_results_20280401.csv (initial eval outputs), prompt_set_finwave_v2.txt

Next steps (I propose):
1) Redwood runs a 48-hour batch eval across the three models + quantization variants above using your prompt set (we'll generate the CSV and a short slide deck). (Action: Redwood)
2) FinWave reviews the attached prompts & adds any privacy-sensitive examples to redact (Action: FinWave)
3) Quick follow-up call next Tuesday to review results and discuss routing policy + autoscaling (30m) (Action: both)

Can you confirm those next steps and whether Tuesdays at 10am PT works for you?

Thanks — Marissa

Adding some technical context so expectations are clear before the eval run: 

Quick recommendations based on model families:
- Llama-3-13B: Run AWQ (4-bit) and GPTQ (4-bit) variants. AWQ typically keeps instruction-following quality higher; GPTQ is a solid baseline if you need portability across runtimes.
- Mistral-7B-Instruct: GPTQ tends to be fast and cost-efficient; AWQ can be used if we see edge-case regressions on summarization prompts.
- Llama-3-70B: If you want the best quality at scale, run FP8 on H100 as the primary throughput option and keep a float16 or AWQ fallback. FP8 will give the best tokens/sec on H100 but requires the Redwood runtime in FP8 mode (we have this in dedicated but will validate).

Notes about evaluation and measurement:
- We'll compute per-sample deltas vs float16 reference for Rouge-L and a quality score. Flag any sample with >0.12 Rouge-L drop or >0.8 point drop in manual score for human review.
- For classification, we will surface precision/recall and the exact examples causing false negatives so you can triage quickly.
- Throughput numbers will be reported as tokens/sec on H100 (FP8/FP16) and tokens/sec-equivalent for 4-bit quantized runs (AWQ/GPTQ), plus p50/p95 latencies for 1- and 8-request batching patterns.

Caveat: FP8 quality depends on the compilation path and operator support — we'll include a compatibility matrix in the deck (H100-only today; A100 support is experimental).

I will lead the eval run with Neha and push the initial CSV and slide summary by Friday EOD.

-Rishi
